tasks.short: Search and summarise literature, analyse study data, write the research report, format references to journal rules, check the manuscript with co-authors, and submit it.

steps.what: Dietitian searches and summarises literature for the research report

loop.input: The research question and an index of papers the dietitian has selected.
loop.output: A summary of what the papers report, with a citation per sentence.
loop.check: Code checks every citation points to an indexed paper and the quoted passage appears in it; sentences without a valid citation are dropped; the dietitian reads the key papers.
loop.stop: One summary per section; if no sentence passes, the dietitian writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Papers use varied terms and designs; a reference list does not say what they found.

steps.what: Dietitian analyses study data and builds tables in a spreadsheet
Dietitian writes the findings and interpretation to communicate research findings
Dietitian formats references and the manuscript to journal rules
Dietitian checks the final manuscript with co-authors
Dietitian submits the publication on the journal's portal

tasks.design: A bounded step summarises the papers the dietitian selected, with a citation per sentence that code checks against the paper; the dietitian reads the key papers. The analysis set out in the study plan runs as a fixed script on the study data and produces the tables, instead of building them by hand. A reference manager formats citations to the journal's style. Writing the findings and interpretation stays with the dietitian; no model writes the results section.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was summarised, tables built and references formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models summarise selected papers with checkable citations; scripts and reference managers do the rest.
tasks.still_hard: Journals reject on design, not on formatting.
tasks.human_edge: Saying what the findings mean for patients.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian writes and interprets instead of formatting.

reach.learn: Whether drafts arrive with checked tables and references.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarise selected papers with citations that code checks; reference managers format citations to journal styles.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the manuscript submitted; peer review is outside.
Input contract: study data cleaned and an analysis plan fixed; fallback is building tables by hand.
Writing findings stays with the dietitian.
research_questions: How often does the citation check drop a sentence?

already_counted.description: Dietitian reads the drafted literature summary.

incremental.description: Dietitian writes the analysis script from the study plan.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript as checked with co-authors in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short reports with few sources; high: reviews with many papers and tables.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read applications, interview and select kitchen workers, train them on diets, hygiene and allergens, supervise meal preparation and serving, record training sign-offs, and plan shifts.

steps.what: Dietitian reads applications sent by e-mail
Dietitian interviews and selects workers who plan, prepare and serve meals
Dietitian trains workers on diets, hygiene and allergens
Dietitian supervises meal preparation and serving
Dietitian records training and hygiene sign-offs on paper
Dietitian plans kitchen shifts in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Applications arrive in the recruitment system ({ATS}) with the same fields for each candidate instead of loose e-mails; no software ranks candidates. Training and hygiene sign-offs are ticked on a checklist per worker in the learning system ({LMS}), which shows who is due for a refresher. Shifts are planned in the rostering module ({HCM}) with availability and skills. Interviewing, training and supervising stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications came by e-mail, sign-offs were on paper and shifts in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Recruitment, learning and rostering systems are standard in hospitals.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching a cook why a texture-modified meal matters for a patient who cannot swallow.

reach.learn: Whether refresher training is on time.

evidence.claim: Recruitment, learning and rostering systems can hold applications, sign-offs and shifts.
AI used to select candidates is high-risk under Annex III; here no software ranks candidates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the vacancy to shifts planned; contracts are outside.
Input contract: systems run by HR; fallback is e-mail, paper and spreadsheets.
Selection, training and supervision stay with the dietitian.
research_questions: Are hygiene refreshers done on time more often?

incremental.description: Dietitian keeps skills in the rostering module current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a stable team; high: high turnover with many new workers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather evidence on nutrition labeling, fortification or school standards, consult colleagues, decide recommendations, draft the policy response, check it, and submit it to the public consultation.

steps.what: Dietitian gathers evidence on nutrition labeling, food fortification or school nutrition standards

loop.input: The consultation question and an index of studies and guidelines the dietitian selected.
loop.output: A summary of the evidence with a citation per sentence.
loop.check: Code checks every citation points to an indexed source and the quoted passage appears in it; sentences without a valid citation are dropped; the dietitian reads the key sources.
loop.stop: One summary per question; if no sentence passes, the dietitian writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sources differ in design and terms; a reading list does not say what they found.

steps.what: Dietitian consults colleagues and professional bodies
Dietitian decides the recommendations regarding public policy
Dietitian writes the consultation response

loop.input: The decided recommendations and the checked evidence summary.
loop.output: A draft response in the consultation's format.
loop.check: Code checks every factual claim cites a source from the evidence summary and every recommendation appears; the dietitian rewrites and approves.
loop.stop: Up to two redrafts; then the dietitian writes the response.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each consultation asks different questions; a template cannot argue the case.

steps.what: Dietitian checks the final response
Dietitian submits the response on the government consultation portal

tasks.design: A bounded step summarises the studies and guidelines the dietitian selected, with a citation per sentence that code checks. After consulting colleagues and deciding the recommendations, a second bounded step drafts the response from the recommendations and the checked summary; code checks every claim cites a source and every recommendation appears. The dietitian rewrites and checks the response and submits it personally. Deciding what to recommend stays with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was summarised and responses written from scratch for each consultation.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models summarise and draft from selected sources with checkable citations.
tasks.still_hard: Policy turns on politics and cost as much as evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing for school standards in terms a minister will accept.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian decides and rewrites instead of compiling.

reach.learn: Whether responses arrive before the deadline.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarise and draft from selected sources with citations that code checks.

assumptions: Boundary: from the policy consultation to the response submitted; the policy decision is outside.
Input contract: sources selected by the dietitian; fallback is writing by hand.
Recommendations are decided by the dietitian.
No personal data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted response survives the rewrite?

already_counted.description: Dietitian reads the drafted evidence summary.

incremental.description: Dietitian builds the source index for each consultation.

approvals.approved_version: The response as checked by the dietitian in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new topics with few sources; high: topics with much evidence.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review production, cost and waste figures, set budget and priorities, lead team meetings and coordinate with wards, plan rosters, check food safety records, and handle staff and quality issues.

steps.what: Dietitian reviews meal production, cost and waste figures from spreadsheets
Dietitian sets budget and priorities to manage the food service department
Dietitian leads team meetings and coordinates with wards
Dietitian plans staff rosters in a spreadsheet
Dietitian checks paper food safety and temperature records
Dietitian handles staff and quality issues

tasks.design: Meal counts from the food ordering system and costs from finance ({ERP}) feed a dashboard ({BI}) with production, cost per meal and waste per ward, so the dietitian does not build spreadsheets. Rosters are planned in the rostering module ({HCM}). Fridge and freezer temperatures are logged by sensors and kitchen checks are ticked on tablets, so the dietitian reviews exceptions instead of paper lists. Setting priorities, leading the team and handling issues stay with the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were compiled in spreadsheets and food safety records kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Food service systems feed dashboards; temperature sensors log fridges automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Waste figures depend on staff weighing leftovers.
tasks.human_edge: Getting cooks and ward staff to agree on meal times.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian acts on exceptions instead of compiling figures.

reach.learn: Whether waste per ward is visible.

evidence.claim: Temperature sensors can log fridges and freezers for food safety records; food service data can feed dashboards.

assumptions: Boundary: from period figures to issues handled; menu design is outside.
Input contract: meal and cost data in systems; fallback is spreadsheets and paper.
Priorities and staff issues stay with the dietitian.
Kitchen staff tick checks on tablets in about the time paper took.
research_questions: Does waste per meal fall when it is visible per ward?

incremental.description: Dietitian acts on sensor alerts outside planned checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small kitchen; high: a large hospital kitchen with many wards.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The dietitian keeps writing findings, selecting and training staff, deciding policy recommendations and running the department; literature compiling, spreadsheets and paper records shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A dietitian with more time for research and the team.
